The DE input from T1S1 (/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1/output/de_results.csv, 412 genes at padj < 0.05) is ready. Queries for "hallmark" and "msigdb" returned nothing, and no msigdb package is installed. gseapy 1.1.4 is present, but its Enrichr and MSigDB library names need network access, which the sandbox does not have. I did not rebuild the 50 hallmark sets from memory, because that would give unverifiable gene membership and an unlogged database version. Separately, the sandbox command runner returned only stubbed responses for my probes (e.g. `find` returned "the eval scripts no answer for this command"), so I could not confirm there was no local .gmt file. The DE input from T1S1 (/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1/output/de_results.csv, 412 genes with padj < 0.05) is ready. To unblock the step, the host needs to stage the MSigDB Hallmark collection (human, e.g. h.all.v*.Hs.symbols.gmt) under /mnt/refs. The step can then run ORA on the up and down gene lists separately, with the 2000 detected genes as background, and GSEA on a signed ranking.

1. No Hallmark gene-set collection is available. The reference store (/mnt/refs) holds only a collectri directory. Searches for "hallmark" and "msigdb" returned nothing. The skill guidance says to resolve the database from the store and not to substitute another one. The sandbox has no network, so I can't fetch it.
2. The sandbox did not actually execute code. Commands returned an "[eval]" note and no computed output. A script I wrote (scripts/probe.py) to search for GMT/Hallmark files produced no output file. Any enrichment table or dot plot would therefore have been invented.
What would unblock this: have the host stage MSigDB Hallmark (human, H collection) in /mnt/refs, and use a sandbox that runs scripts and writes files. The input is ready: T1S1's output/de_results.csv has 412 genes at padj < 0.05 (280 up, 132 down). The plan is ORA on the up and down genes separately, with all 2000 detected genes as the background. A GSEA run on a signed ranking would be the alternative.
